subject: HelioHealth — eval execution & scoring design
messages:
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Eva Santos <eva.santos@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: HelioHealth kickoff — model validation discovery

Thanks again for the time today, Eva — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the trial: 

Takeaways from the call:
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant for inbound patient messages (short clinical summaries + recommended disposition).
- Data available: ~40k de-identified message/triage pairs; Helio can provide a 1k sample for initial run.
- Success metrics: acceptable precision on urgent flags (target >= 92%), human-review F1 target ~0.86, and low false negative rate for red flags.
- Regulatory note: dataset will be delivered under DTAs; logs must be retained for 90 days and filtered for PHI.

Our recommended approach on Redwood for the pilot:
1) Bench models: redwood-curated instruction-tuned family (meta-llama-2-7b-instruct, redwood-mistral-8b) plus a 16-bit quantized LLM for cost baseline.
2) Run customer-specific eval harness using the Helio sample set and our scoring template. We'll produce per-case flags (TP/FP/FN), precision/recall, and a confusion breakdown for dispositions.
3) Validate prompt sensitivity with a small prompt bank (we'll run 30 prompt variants).

Action items — please: 
- Share the 1k sample (CSV or JSONL) and a column description. We prefer a JSONL with fields: message_id, patient_text, gold_disposition, priority_flag.
- Confirm whether Helio wants experimental caching/batching enabled (we can tune for latency vs cost).

I attached a short schema and our draft playbook for execution. If this looks good I’ll provision the eval run and send a kickoff calendar invite for next Tue.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We can share the 1k de-id sample by Friday via the Drive link (I’ll upload a JSONL). Columns will match the format you listed.
- Priority flags: Helio has two levels (urgent, routine). For your scoring template, please treat urgent as the primary positive class for precision computation.
- For prompt variants: can you include a narrow instruction that asks the model to return a single disposition token ("escalate", "schedule", "educate") as well as an open-text explanation? We need structured outputs for downstream routing.
- We are risk-averse on retention — 90-day logs ok but only if they are encrypted and access-controlled.

We’re OK to kickoff next Tue (14 Oct) if provisioning is quick. Also, curious on estimated runway cost for a 1k-run across the three model variants you suggested.

—Eva
Eva Santos
Head of Clinical Ops, HelioHealth

On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 9:18 AM Eva Santos <eva.santos@heliohealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
> - We can share the 1k de-id sample by Friday via the Drive link (I’ll upload a JSONL).
> - Priority flags: Helio has two levels (urgent, routine).

Perfect — quick answers below and an expanded scoring checklist attached.

Scoring & output format notes:
- Primary metric: urgent precision (precision_urgent) — we’ll compute: TP_urgent / (TP_urgent + FP_urgent). Target >= 0.92.
- Secondary: macro-F1 across disposition tokens (escalate/schedule/educate).
- Allowed model outputs: one token from the set {escalate, schedule, educate}. If the model outputs free text we’ll post-process with a simple mapping table (attached).
- Regression guardrails: we’ll run a baseline comparison vs last-month prod predictions (if Helio provides 5k prod-sample lines). Any drop >3 percentage points on primary metric triggers a stop-and-review.

Estimated cost (rough):
- meta-llama-2-7b-instruct: $45–$70 for 1k cases (profiled with 512 token response limit).
- redwood-mistral-8b: $55–$85.
- 16-bit quant baseline: $25–$40.

Next steps I’ll take after we get the sample:
1) Upload the run manifest and prompt bank (I attached helio_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) to the shared Drive.
2) Provision a secured eval workspace in your VPC (or hosted with strict KMS) depending on your preference.
3) Kickoff run on Tue 14 Oct and deliver a scored report within 48 hours of completion.

Attaching: helio_prompt_set_v1.jsonl and the scoring_checklist.csv. Linking the HubSpot deal for reference.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: helio_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, scoring_checklist.csv

Great — thanks for the upload, Marcus. Confirming the plan and a couple of implementation details: 
- We’ll provision a private eval workspace in the Helio VPC using the cross-account S3 option you suggested; this will ensure logs/data never touch our hosted buckets. Laura will own the infra setup and the KMS config.
- Scoring: we’ll include the "needs_human" bucket in the report and provide a small UI export for those cases.
- Timeline: kickoff Tue 14 Oct, runs complete by Thu 16 Oct EOD, report delivered by Fri 17 Oct.
- Risk note: if we see quality regression vs your prod baseline >3% on urgent precision we’ll pause additional runs and schedule a review with Helio engineering.

Next actions for Helio: share cross-account role ARN or S3 presigned details + confirm KMS policy (Laura will send a checklist).

I’ll send a calendar invite and the run manifest shortly. Thanks — excited to get this started.
